insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Varies by plan (Silver/Gold/Platinum; Individual/Family Floater/Family First). Examples: Individual & Family Floater: Silver 2L/3L; Gold 5L-50L; Platinum 15L-1Cr. Family First: Base SI per person + Floater SI (as per Annexure II).

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Re-fill benefit Reinstate up to base Sum Insured. Applicable for same & different illness as well
great.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table (Silver/Gold/Platinum tables)
great.explanation: Sum insured can be reinstated up to the base Sum Insured and can be used for the same or a different illness. This improves claim-paying ability within the same policy year after the base cover is used.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months (under gold & platinum Plans)/ 36 months (under Silver Plans) of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months (Gold/Platinum) or 36 months (Silver) of continuous coverage from first policy inception. This is broadly in line with typical retail health insurance waiting periods.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, except for accidents. This is a standard market condition and mainly affects early claims for non-accident illnesses.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: For all Insured Persons who are above 45 years of Age as on the date of inception of the First Policy with Us... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are excluded for 24 months for insured persons who are above 45 years at first policy inception. This delays coverage for listed conditions and is common in many plans.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will pay above mentioned Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for period up to 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days before admission. This helps pay for diagnostics and consultations leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for up to 90 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 90 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room rent Shared Room or 1% of the Base Sum Insured per day
bad.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table: Individual & Family Floater Silver Plan (Renewal only)
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited to Shared Room or 1% of the Base Sum Insured per day. Choosing a higher room category can lead to large out-of-pocket costs and may also reduce other linked hospital charges.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a Hospital room where the room category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligibility as specified in the Policy Schedule, then We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses... (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses
bad.explanation: If you take a room above your eligible category/limit, the insurer pays only a pro-rated portion of associated medical expenses using (Eligible Room Rent / Actual Room Rent). This can sharply reduce the claim payout beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement... 6.2.14 Co-payment The Insured Person will bear a predetermined percentage of the admissible claim amounts subject to the Co-payment option chosen by You in the Proposal Form and / or Information Summary Sheet
bad.explanation: A co-payment applies based on the option chosen in the proposal form and/or information summary sheet, meaning you bear a predetermined percentage of each admissible claim. This directly increases your out-of-pocket share on every claim where co-pay is opted/selected.

unclear.name: NCB
unclear.quote: If the Insured Persons covered on a Family Floater Policy... Renew... by splitting... then We will provide the credit of the accumulated Cumulative Bonus to the split Policy reduced proportionately... In case the Base Sum Insured under the Policy is reduced at the time of Renewal, the applicable accumulated Cumulative Bonus shall also be reduced in proportion to the Base Sum Insured.
unclear.explanation: Cumulative Bonus is reduced proportionately if the policy is split or if the Base Sum Insured is reduced at renewal. The wording does not clarify whether the bonus resets/reduces on a claim, so the overall NCB impact cannot be fully assessed from this extract.
